diagram_math_checks.justification: The Example specifies S={s}, A(s)={a,b}. The single circular s and two rectangular a,b nodes match these sets. The arrows s→a and s→b represent available choices, not extra MDP states or transitions. Node identities, shapes and directed endpoints are unchanged.

The Example states deterministic returns to s with reward 1 under a and 3 under b. In def-finite-markov-decision-process, p(s′,rho|s,a) is joint mass on next state and reward. Thus the two curved arrows a→s and b→s labeled p(s,1|s,a)=1 and p(s,3|s,b)=1 are exactly the original model. There are three drawing vertices and four directed drawing edges; the two action rectangles are choice devices, so the MDP still has one state. No probabilities, rewards, or arrow directions changed.

def-policy-bellman-operator and def-bellman-optimality-operator place gamma on the continuation term only; the Example uses gamma=1/2. The diagram depicts only original immediate rewards 1,3, consistent with Verification 1.1: v=1+v/2 or 3+v/2, hence fixed points 2,6. Verification 2.1 shifts rewards to 3,5 and values to 6,10; the unchanged Remarks accurately describe that change without suggesting additional discount on the edge rewards.
